headline: Library Book Returned After 40 Years With Three-Page Apology, Pressed Flower
summary: Copy of 'The Joy of Cooking' checked out in 1984 arrives by mail with handwritten letter describing 'decades of low-grade guilt.'
content:
The Hartwell District Public Library received an unexpected delivery Tuesday: a well-worn copy of 'The Joy of Cooking' that had been checked out on March 15, 1984, and never returned—until now.

Accompanying the book was a three-page handwritten letter and a pressed daisy, both tucked inside the front cover.

"Dear Library," the letter begins. "I have carried this book, and the guilt of keeping it, through four apartments, two marriages, and one cross-country move. I am returning it now because I am 67 years old and I have decided to stop being the kind of person who keeps library books."

The letter, signed only "A Reformed Borrower," goes on to describe how the anonymous patron originally intended to return the book "after trying just a few more recipes" and then "somehow it just... stayed." The writer expresses particular remorse about the beef stroganoff chapter, which shows signs of heavy use.

"I made that stroganoff probably 200 times over the years," the letter reads. "Every single time, I thought about returning this book. I want you to know that."

Head Librarian Constance Murray noted that under the library's old fine system, the book would have accrued approximately $847 in late fees. However, the library eliminated late fees in 2019.

"We're just glad to have it back," Murray said. "Although I have to admit, the letter made the whole staff a little emotional. We've all kept a library book too long at some point. This person just... kept it longer."

The daisy, Murray noted, appears to be from the same era as the checkout date. "It's been pressed flat for 40 years. That's dedication to guilt."

The library plans to display the book and letter (with personal details redacted) as part of an upcoming exhibit on "Books That Came Home."
author: Ellen Park, Arts & Culture
